# T4 synthetic engine consumer acceptance specimens

The following **synthetic consumer specimens** define what #25 asks #11 to exercise for each supported tuple. They are not vendor results, measurements or new catalog records. All run identity fields specified in [the framework handoff](../../research/T4-agents-integrations/agent-framework.md#engine-consumer-acceptance-specification-11-to-25) must be supplied from actual artifacts before recording an observed result. Record the exact sanitized request and response, engine flags, endpoint, parser, exit/error status and source/reproduction date. Unknown or unexercised tuples stay unknown. Route runtime evidence placement through #36; no product is claimed to have passed these cases.

| Case | Synthetic input / response specimen | Required consumer check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FC-1 single tool round trip | A no-side-effect `lookup_fixture` tool with arguments schema `{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string","enum":["alpha"]}},"required":["key"],"additionalProperties":false}`; request lookup of `alpha`; simulated result `{"value":"fixture-only"}` | Parse a supported tool-call envelope, require the declared name and schema-valid arguments, correlate the returned call ID to the submitted tool result, and continue the conversation. Natural-language mention of a tool does not satisfy this case. |
| FC-2 malformed arguments | Inject a synthetic call with arguments `{"key":7}` or undeclared `delete_fixture` | Consumer rejects it before dispatch; no real tool is called. This tests the consumer validator, not engine generation quality. |
| FC-3 request controls | Repeat FC-1 with each requested automatic, required, named and disabled tool-choice mode | Record each mode separately with its exact endpoint request. A documented unsupported control is unsupported only within that tuple; an untested/undocumented control remains unknown. No silent downgrade is counted as support. |
| FC-4 streaming and parallel calls | Feed two synthetic call IDs with interleaved argument fragments; separately exercise non-streaming output | Reassemble by call ID and validate complete arguments before dispatch; preserve tool-result correlation. Record streaming and parallel support separately; passing non-streaming single-call FC-1 does not establish either. |
| FC-5 structured output | Request `{"type":"object","properties":{"answer":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["answer"],"additionalProperties":false}`; synthetic valid `{"answer":1}` and invalid `{"answer":"one"}` | Consumer accepts/rejects according to the declared schema; separately record the engine grammar/backend's supported schema subset, refusals and truncation. Valid JSON alone does not establish strict schema enforcement. |
| FC-6 changed or incomplete tuple | Reuse an FC-1 result after changing parser/template, model revision, quantization, adapter, endpoint or streaming mode; alternatively omit one required identity field | Do not inherit the previous result automatically. Require matching eligible evidence or mark the new tuple unknown. Keep original evidence immutable for saved-build re-evaluation. |

The next runtime exercise is jointly scoped with #11/#36 owners after selecting concrete tuples and approved evidence storage. This specification supplies request/response acceptance criteria; it does not complete the runtime exercise or invent a versioned build contract.
